title: Control Snapshotter — Scheduled Attestations for Retention & Residency
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Build a scheduled 'Control Snapshotter' that automatically materializes time-bound attestations for data residency and retention controls. The snapshotter will collect configuration state, custody metadata, and evidence artifacts across Redwood deployments on a schedule (daily/weekly/monthly) and emit a tamper-evident attestation bundle suitable for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 auditors.

Problem: Currently our evidence collection is ad-hoc and manual for audits. Customers must rely on support or run manual exports. This creates risk during audits, increases lead time for compliance reviews, and makes it hard for customers to demonstrate continuous compliance for retention and residency controls.

Scope: - Map the set of retention/residency controls to observable signals (S3 region tags, object lifecycle rules, DB TTL configs, VPC export markers). - Implement scheduled collectors that snapshot control state and correlated logs. - Produce an attestation bundle (manifest + artifacts + signed checksum) per customer and per region. - Expose download/verification UI in Console and an API endpoint for programmatic retrieval. - Include primitives for customer-specified retention exceptions and an audit trail for overrides.
background: Recent SOC 2 readiness assessments highlighted long turnaround times to gather retention evidence for customers with multi-region deployments. Competing platforms ship 'scheduled attestation' features; to maintain our production-first differentiation we need an automated, auditable flow that ties control settings to discrete exportable artifacts and minimizes manual steps for our compliance teams and customers.
goals: 1) Deliver a repeatable, scheduled export that maps controls to artifacts; 2) Reduce manual evidence collection time during audits by 80%; 3) Provide tamper-evident bundles that third-party auditors can verify independently; 4) Surface exceptions and policy drift in Console within 24 hours.
success_metrics:
- Time to produce full retention/residency evidence bundle reduced from avg 5 business days to <= 0.5 business days.
- 80% of audit requests satisfied by automated bundle without manual support.
- Snapshot bundles verified by an internal compliance mock audit with no findings in first run.
acceptance_criteria: Control mapping document completed and reviewed by Security & Compliance
Collectors implemented for object storage, DB retention configs, and network geofencing markers across 3 cloud regions
Attestation bundle format defined (manifest.json + artifacts folder + sha256sum + signature) and verified by compliance
Console UI shows last snapshot time, bundle status, and allows download for a 365-day retention window
API endpoint authenticated and returns signed bundle with a clear verification flow
Audit trail records timestamp, actor, and reason for any retention override
tasks: Map all retention/residency controls to technical signals (owner: PM)
Design attestation bundle schema and signing process (owner: Security)
Implement collector Lambda/agent for object stores (owner: ENG)
Implement DB retention config collector and TTL snapshotter (owner: ENG)
Pipeline to aggregate artifacts and create bundle (owner: ENG)
Console UX: snapshot status, download, and verification hints (owner: Design + ENG)
End-to-end QA including compliance mock audit (owner: PM + Security)
Docs and runbook for support and customer-facing guide (owner: Docs)
Rollout plan and migration path for customers with existing manual evidence (owner: PM)
Add metrics to Observe: bundle generation latency, failures, and CHURN of overrides (owner: ENG)
Incident playbook: stale snapshot remediation and re-attestation (owner: SRE)
decision_record: We will use per-customer key signing (KMS-backed) for bundle signatures to avoid cross-customer coupling. Retention exceptions will be recorded as immutable events in the audit log rather than modifying historical snapshots. Initial rollout will support daily snapshots; weekly/monthly schedules are reserved for low-activity tiers.

notes: Trade-offs considered: embedding full artifacts (heavy) vs references to artifact storage (lighter). We chose a hybrid: small artifacts embedded, large artifacts referenced by signed URLs with integrity hashes. Long-term we may integrate with retention-ledger microservice for immutable storage.
estimated_cost_impact: Moderate engineering effort in Q2; predictable ROI via reduced manual audit hours
